story: 01 / Reference implementation
A farm designed to be read, tested and replicated.
Three maize treatments, one monitored fish system, an aquaponics loop and a human-supervised computational layer share the same evidence trail.
02 / Arrival sequence
The visitor route is part of the research design.
A single circulation spine lets visitors read the system in order: human oversight, computational infrastructure, experiments and biological loops.
03 / Computational field layer
Computing is physically distributed across the farm.
A phenotyping portal, autonomous scout, smart valves, fertigation controller, field gateway, RTK base and UAV dock connect sensing to local decisions and bounded actuation.
04 / Experimental field
Three plots turn prior maize research into a live protocol.

The shared field geometry is now instrumented by repeatable imaging, paired-depth sensing, flow metering and plot-level actuator nodes so biological comparison and computational control remain linked.
05 / Aquatic sensing
The fish pond is an experimental subsystem, not an ornament.
Feeding behavior, dissolved oxygen, pH, temperature, underwater video and control actions are recorded together; a small inspection ROV makes subsurface observation explicit.
06 / Biological loop
The greenhouse makes the water and data cycles visible.
The DWC loop now includes a vision rail, PLC/pump supervision and repeatable sensing, connecting crop response to circulation state rather than treating the greenhouse as a static display.
07 / Human-supervised control
Automation is bounded by a physical and procedural human gate.
Server racks, local networking, operator displays, weather context, UAV/RTK support and manual override make the farm's computing infrastructure visible and inspectable.
08 / The sample-room idea
Reference Farm 001 is a blueprint with a living example attached.
The goal is not to prescribe one brand of hardware, but to make the interfaces between sensing, computing, actuation and verification concrete enough to copy.

cloud.name: Partly cloudy
cloud.action: Lower solar load. Crop-water model reduces short-term evapotranspiration demand.

rain.name: Light rain
rain.action: Rain input detected. Routine irrigation is suspended; drainage and pond inflow are watched.

storm.name: Convective storm
storm.action: High wind + heavy rain: UAV launch inhibited, gantry parked, irrigation locked out, human review required.

heat.name: Hot / high ET
heat.action: High evapotranspiration risk. Soil-water forecast shortens the next decision horizon.

wind.name: Dry wind event
wind.action: Wind threshold exceeded for small UAVs. Ground sensing stays active; crop-motion compensation is enabled.

fog.name: Cool morning fog
fog.action: Low-visibility state. Vision confidence is down-weighted until contrast recovers; soil and water sensors continue normally.
